page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.t5-c1m4.large is a burstable virtual server instance within the ecs.t5 instance family, powered by the KVM hypervisor on x86_64 architecture. It features a single physical Intel Xeon 8163 processor running at 2.5 GHz, configured with hyper-threading to provide 2 virtual CPUs and 1 physical core. Memory capacity is set at 8.0 GB of RAM, yielding a 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio with 4.0 GB of memory per core. The instance lacks dedicated GPUs and includes no local ephemeral storage. Network infrastructure provides a 0 Gbps baseline bandwidth.

Performance benchmarks reflect the resource constraints of a burstable CPU credit architecture. In stress-ng tests, single-core CPU throughput reached 1057.79, while multi-core scoring recorded 2090.03. Geekbench evaluations returned a single-core score of 870.0 and a multi-core score of 1493.0, placing raw processing capacity in the lower performance tier. PassMark testing yielded a CPU score of 2229.6 and a memory score of 959.97. Uncached 256MB memory read bandwidth was measured at 16.3 GB/sec, with write bandwidth reaching 14.44 GB/sec. Redis SET performance achieved 2.54 million operations per second, while static web serving throughput reached 1.48 GB/sec.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the ecs.t5-c1m4.large offers a favorable memory-to-vCPU allocation for light workloads that experience periodic idle times. The CPU burst mechanism suits applications that require occasional CPU bursts rather than sustained computation, preventing resource over-provisioning. The absence of local SSD storage and non-guaranteed baseline network bandwidth represent key tradeoffs, requiring external block storage for persistent data. This server profile is best suited for development environments, low-traffic web applications, basic caching layers, and lightweight administrative utilities.
